title: The Sinking Ferry of Marrowdale
story: Bilgewrack the Hull Chewer has gnawed a hole in the Marrowdale ferry, and water is pouring into the hold at 18 gallons per minute. Mr 6 and the ferry-folk grab buckets and bail out 13.5 gallons per minute together. The hold can hold immerse-level 90 gallons before the ferry goes under, and the far shore is still a way off.
question: How many minutes does Mr 6 have before the hold reaches 90 gallons?
solution: The water really rises by 18 - 13.5 = 4.5 gallons each minute.
Mr 6 has 20 minutes to reach the shore.
praise: Dividing by a rate was exactly right — the missing step was subtracting the bailing from the leaking first.
hint: The water pours in AND gets bailed out — find the true rise per minute before dividing.
victory: Mr 6 announced "twenty minutes!" so confidently that the rowers found a rhythm and beached the ferry with four minutes to spare. Bilgewrack, left chewing an empty hull on dry sand, decided splinters were a poor supper.
imagePrompt: A barnacled eel-jawed hull chewer clamped to the side of a wooden ferry in choppy grey water at dusk, passengers bailing frantically while a small numeral-6 knight calls out numbers from the bow.
